lines.name: laplaceL1_line1.mp3
lines.spoken: In this lecture we see what the Laplace transform does for circuits, and find three transforms straight from the definition. Then you'll try one yourself.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line2.mp3
lines.spoken: A capacitor or an inductor gives us a differential equation.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line3.mp3
lines.spoken: The transform turns each derivative into multiplication by s.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line4.mp3
lines.spoken: So the differential equation becomes algebra, and the initial condition comes along for free.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line5.mp3
lines.spoken: Here is the definition. Multiply f of t by e to the minus s t, and integrate. s is complex: sigma plus j omega.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line6.mp3
lines.spoken: We start the integral at zero minus, just before t equals zero. That captures an impulse at t equals zero, and the energy already stored in the circuit.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line7.mp3
lines.spoken: First, the unit step. It equals one for positive t, so only the exponential is left.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line8.mp3
lines.spoken: Integrate, then evaluate between the two limits.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line9.mp3
lines.spoken: At the upper limit the exponential goes to zero, if the real part of s is positive.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line10.mp3
lines.spoken: At the lower limit the exponential is one, which leaves one over s.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line11.mp3
lines.spoken: Next, e to the minus a t. The two exponents add, to s plus a.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line12.mp3
lines.spoken: The same steps give one over s plus a, if the real part of s is greater than minus a.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line13.mp3
lines.spoken: Last, the impulse. Zero minus keeps it inside the limits, and it sifts out the exponential at t equals zero.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line14.mp3
lines.spoken: e to the zero is one, so the impulse transforms to one.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line15.mp3
lines.spoken: Three integrals give three pairs. From here on, we read transforms from the table.

lines.name: laplaceL1_line16.mp3
lines.spoken: Your turn. On paper, find the transform of cosine omega t. Hint: use Euler's formula.
